to see the stars, one by one,
and pick the prettiest of them all
she talks and talks all day,

parrafos: The pineapple is from the island.
A house made from a box!
Sol puts the tablet down and goes out to play.
Me siento junto a mi amigo.
Le echo un poco de agua.
Le pregunto primero a mi amigo.

My grandma Inés is special. Nobody knows how to do as many things as she does. Abu makes the best rice with sausages in the world! She puts in lots of sausages. So many that my dad says it's sausages with rice instead of rice with sausages. Abu also knows the funniest songs. Besides singing and cooking, Abu knows a lot of things. She knows the best games in the world. Our favorite game is hide-and-seek.

She almost always hides in the closet. Sometimes she stands behind the bathroom door. I prefer to hide under her bed. It is tall and has a cushion underneath. Abu says it is my special cushion. She puts it there so I am comfortable while she finds me. But the best thing about Abu is her hugs. She gives the best hugs in the world. When Abu hugs me, I feel happy and safe.

Ants are very interesting insects. They can live underground, on the ground, or in trees. Ants are very organized. They work together like a team. They share the tasks. Each one does a different job. Ants live in large groups. The place where they live is called an anthill. Each anthill is led by a queen. Her job is to lay many eggs. Many worker ants also live in the anthill. They are the most common and the hardest working. They take care of the eggs the queen lays. They are also in charge of looking for food. Ants communicate through smells. They smell with their antennae. When they walk, they leave a special scent. That is how they recognize the path back to the anthill. The scent also warns them when there is danger. The next time you see a line of ants, try to follow them. You will have fun watching them.

What a beautiful rabbit Sofía has! It is white as cotton. Its ears are long and furry. It has four short legs with yellow spots. Its eyes are black and shiny. It eats green leaves like lettuce. It also likes fruit very much. When Sofía comes home, the rabbit gets very happy. First, it runs toward her, hopping. Then it starts to run all over the place. One day, Sofía's neighbor went to work in her garden. She had planted some carrots. When she arrived, she found the rabbit eating the leaves. She tried to catch it, but she could not. The rabbit was very fast. It slipped through a hole under the fence of Sofía's house.
If the neighbor had not told her, Sofía would never have realized how clever her rabbit was.

Mumo the monkey is going for a walk. He looks at the map to see how to get to the museum. He gets on his motorbike and looks at the street. Oh no, his map falls and Mumo doesn't know! He looks at butterflies, he is distracted. When he realized it, he was already lost. He looks in his backpack, oh no, the map is not there! Mumo doesn't know how he will get there. So he asks what the way is. Climb the mountain, you will see a windmill. Right there on the right is the museum. Thank you, thank you very much! he says to Romeo. He goes along the road and reaches the museum. With a coin, he pays for his ticket. He looks at the details with his two little eyes, and after a while, you can hear his scream:
Ahhhhh! Mumo runs and runs, he leaves the museum. The mummy museum scares him a lot.
primero-es-04.notas: El original dice 'Memo' en el último párrafo (probable error de tipeo por 'Mumo'); se tradujo como Mumo. Es un poema con rima: la traducción es literal y no conserva la rima.

parrafos: Popi lives in Mali, a country on the African continent.
Mirsa lives in Puerto Rico, an island in the Caribbean.
Popi has a mom, a dad, and a sister. Mirsa has a mom, a grandma, and a brother.
Popi eats mango with his mom. Mirsa cooks with her grandma.
Popi runs on the savanna. Mirsa plays at the beach.
They both look at the stars.
Popi and Mirsa are friends under the same sky.
I say it in my letters.
primero-es-06.notas: Poema: traducción literal, no conserva la rima.

parrafos: Lía takes a pear and bread to school.
Before eating, she washes her hands.
Her friend Leo does not have a napkin.
Lía gives him one of hers.
The two of them eat under a tree.
Afterward, they put the leftovers in the right place.
Lía smiles: eating well and taking care of the yard make recess happy.
Tomás arrives at a new school.
In the yard he sees two kids with a ball.
After a while, Sara arrives, and she wants to play too.
Everyone plays and no one is left out.
When the bell rings, Tomás already has new friends.
A toad lives by the lake.
One morning he finds a can near the water.
The can blocks a snail's path.
The toad calls Lola, who is walking with her dad.
Lola tells her dad, and he picks up the can carefully.
Lola learns that a clean lake is a home for many animals.
Bruno brings a drum to school.
His grandmother taught him a bomba rhythm.
In class, Bruno plays: boom, boom, ta!
His friends follow the rhythm by clapping.
A girl says that in her home they listen to different music.
Bruno invites her to show it.
The class discovers that every family has special sounds.
In the end, everyone creates a rhythm together.
Clara keeps lids, boxes, and paper.
She wants to make a toy boat.
First she cuts a paper sail with an adult's help.
Then she places the sail on a small box.
Clara changes the base to a wider one.
Clara discovers that trying a different idea can solve a problem.
Diego wants to know why it rains.
He looks at a picture on the tablet, but he does not understand the message.
His teacher shows him a science page for kids.
There he sees drawings of clouds and drops.
Diego compares the pictures and asks a question.
The teacher explains how to check whether a page is trustworthy.
Diego learns that not everything that appears on a screen is correct.
Lucía plants a flower in the garden.
Every day she gives it a little water.
Lucía is afraid the flower will break.
With her grandfather's help, she builds a small barrier so the soil does not wash away.
When the sun comes out, the flower is still standing strong.
Lucía smiles: taking care of a plant also means observing what it needs.
Martín wants to play with his tablet all afternoon.
His sister suggests going out to the park.
First they walk. Then they run after a ball and rest under a tree.
When they get back home, Martín drinks some water and tells how good he felt.
He decides to set aside a little time every day to move and play outdoors.
